questions.stem: Sketch the graph of f(x) = cosh(x). Which of the following is true about the graph?

choices.A: It has a horizontal asymptote at y = -1.
choices.B: It decreases for all x values.
choices.D: It approaches infinity as x approaches infinity.

questions.solution: The hyperbolic cosine function, cosh(x), has a graph resembling an exponential growth function. It is always positive and approaches infinity as x increases. Therefore, option D is correct.
questions.explanation: Cosh(x) does not have a horizontal asymptote at y = -1 (A) or pass through the origin (B). It also does not decrease for all x values (C); it grows without bound in both directions.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake is to confuse cosh(x) with sinh(x), which has a horizontal asymptote at y = 0.

questions.stem: Sketch the graph of g(x) = sinh(x). Which of the following is true about the graph?

choices.B: It approaches zero as x approaches infinity.

questions.solution: The hyperbolic sine function, sinh(x), is an odd function, meaning sinh(-x) = -sinh(x). This property makes option C correct.
questions.explanation: Sinh(x) does not have vertical asymptotes (A) or approach zero as x approaches infinity (B). Its range is all real numbers, not limited to -1 and 1 (D).
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake is to think that sinh(x) behaves like the regular sine function, which has a limited range.

questions.stem: Sketch the graph of h(x) = tanh(x). Which of the following is true about the graph?

choices.B: Its domain is all real numbers.
choices.C: It approaches 1 as x approaches infinity.
choices.D: It has a range from -1 to 1.

questions.solution: The hyperbolic tangent function, tanh(x), has a range of -1 to 1 and is defined for all real numbers. This makes option D correct.
questions.explanation: Tanh(x) does have vertical asymptotes at x = kπ (where k is an integer) (A). Its domain is indeed all real numbers (B), but it approaches infinity, not 1, as x approaches infinity (C).
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake is to confuse tanh(x) with the regular tangent function, which has a range of (-∞, ∞).

questions.stem: Sketch the graph of j(x) = sech(x). Which of the following is true about the graph?

choices.A: It approaches 1 as x approaches infinity.
choices.B: Its domain is all real numbers except for odd integer multiples of π/2.
choices.C: It has a horizontal asymptote at y = 0.

questions.solution: The hyperbolic secant function, sech(x), approaches 1 as x approaches infinity. This makes option A correct.
questions.explanation: Sech(x) has a domain of all real numbers (B), no horizontal asymptote at y = 0 (C), and is not an even function (D).
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake is to think that sech(x) behaves like the regular secant function, which approaches zero as x approaches infinity.

questions.stem: Sketch the graph of k(x) = csch(x). Which of the following is true about the graph?

choices.B: Its range is all real numbers except for zero.

questions.solution: The hyperbolic cosecant function, csch(x), has a range of all real numbers except for zero and is defined for all real numbers except for odd integer multiples of π. This makes option B correct.
questions.explanation: Csch(x) does have vertical asymptotes at x = kπ (where k is an integer) (A). It approaches infinity, not zero, as x approaches 0 (C). It is not an odd function (D).
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake is to think that csch(x) behaves like the regular cosecant function, which has a range of all real numbers except for zero.

questions.stem: Sketch the graph of l(x) = coth(x). Which of the following is true about the graph?

choices.A: It approaches 1 as x approaches infinity.
choices.B: Its domain is all real numbers except for odd integer multiples of π/2.

questions.solution: The hyperbolic cotangent function, coth(x), has a domain of all real numbers except for odd integer multiples of π/2. This makes option B correct.
questions.explanation: Coth(x) approaches 1 as x approaches infinity (A), has horizontal asymptotes at y = ±1 (C), and is not an even function (D).
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake is to think that coth(x) behaves differently from the regular cotangent function, which has a limited domain.

questions.stem: Sketch the graph of m(x) = sinh(x)/cosh(x). Which of the following is true about the graph?

choices.A: It approaches 1 as x approaches infinity.
choices.B: Its range is all real numbers.
choices.C: It has a vertical asymptote at x = 0.

questions.solution: The hyperbolic tangent function, tanh(x), can be rewritten as sinh(x)/cosh(x). It approaches 1 as x approaches infinity. This makes option A correct.
questions.explanation: Tanh(x) has a range of all real numbers (B), no vertical asymptote at x = 0 (C), and is an odd function, which is true for m(x) as well (D).
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake is to think that sinh(x)/cosh(x) behaves differently from tanh(x), even though they are the same function.
